messages:
maria: Heads up — we've got a couple Dedicated tenants reporting unexpected throttles during tenant B's heavy batch jobs. They have reserved throughput but are still seeing 429s this morning. anyone seen this pattern before?
aj: saw alerts, digging. quick question: are those 429s coming from the quota-enforcer or from the global gateway pool?
devin: sounds like quota-enforcer. Metrics show reserved metrics not being credited for the org while the global pool is being drained by bursts. suspect ordering bug in the routing -> quota check path.
sophie: telemetry timeline: bursts spike at 09:12, tenant A reserved tokens drop to zero at 09:12:30, then A gets 429s even though they should have reserved capacity. link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/tenant-quota/tenantA
kevin: can you post the raw enforcer logs for one of the 429s? we changed how we apply per-key vs per-org buckets in the last rollout (v2).
maria: pasted sample log below from quota-enforcer (sanitized):
```
2026-02-05T09:12:31Z WARN quota-enforcer request denied org=tenantA key=abc123 reason=rate_limit_quota_exceeded pool=global
2026-02-05T09:12:31Z INFO reserved-check org=tenantA reserved_tokens=1000 available=0
2026-02-05T09:12:31Z INFO global-pool available=1200
```
aj: that first line is the issue — reserved-check shows reserved_tokens=1000 but available=0 immediately after. implies race where reserved tokens are allocated but not marked available to the enforcer before the global check.
devin: yep — our refactor had two async calls: fetchReserved(org) and fetchGlobalPool(); we used Promise.all and then applied global-first logic. if global-first wins due to ordering, reserved tokens get skipped.
sophie: what about burst controls? Dedicated tenants should have burst span beyond reserved capacity up to tenant-isolation limit, right?
kevin: design doc: reserved_throughput is guaranteed baseline. tenants may burst into the global spare capacity up to tenant_isolation_limit. but we intentionally prevent other tenants from consuming reserved capacity.
maria: current behavior seems to allow bursts to eat into capacity that should be reserved for other tenants. that's bad.
ops-bot: ALERT: dedicated-tenant-throttle tenant=tenantA severity=warning count=42 link=https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/8472
aj: short-term mitigation: flip a flag to force reserved-first evaluation in quota-enforcer. can we patch quickly?
devin: I can push a small change to ensure reserved tokens are applied before global decrement. patch ready, running unit tests.
infra-bot: Deploy queued: quota-enforcer v2.3.7-canary to canary-hosts (3/6) by devin at 2026-02-05T09:33:12Z
kevin: also we should adjust token-bucket parameters: increase reserved bucket burst_size and refill smoothing window to avoid spiky depletion. e.g. burst_size=5000, refill_rate=200/s, smoothing=10s.
sophie: telemetry will need a new time series: reserved_consumption_by_request_type so we can tell if streaming requests are burning tokens differently.
maria: plan: (1) canary patch reserved-first (devin) (2) increase reserved burst window for affected tenants (kevin) (3) add telemetry panel and alert for reserved_token_drops (sophie) (4) schedule postmortem if other tenants still affected.
aj: I'll also add a regression test in the routing-policy suite that simulates concurrent fetchReserved + global drain.
devin: canary deployed, no regressions in unit/integration tests. will monitor dashboards for the next 30m.
ops-bot: NOTICE: quota-enforcer v2.3.7-canary running on canary-hosts.
kevin: if canary looks good, schedule full rollout with feature flag and gradual host ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%). add kill-switch flag in case we need immediate rollback.
maria: thanks everyone. assigning follow-ups: devin -> prod rollout, kevin -> burst param changes + doc, sophie -> telemetry + alert, aj -> routing-policy regression test. will sync in #eng-oncall if any escalation. :thumbsup:
